newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares drift lower on political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares drift lower on political uncertainty.

text.p: Delhi share prices quoted lower in early trade on Wednesday as speculators sold on reports that a key leader of the ruling United Front coalition had threatened to pull out of the front, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 2.32 points lower at 776.40 after 30 minutes of trade.
Local newspapers said Laloo Prasad Yadav, leader of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, had threatened to withdraw his support to the United Front government.
Yadav, chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, is enmeshed in a $280 million scandal over the use of state animal welfare funds.

The Central Bureau of Investigation recently announced it would prosecute Yadav in the case, marring Gujral's start in office. Yadav has said he is innocent, but party leaders are pressing him to step down.
"Political uncertainty once again had its shadow on the market's sentiment," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.
Reliance Industries dropped 1.25 rupees to 302.00 on speculative selling, brokers said.
State Bank of India dropped 1.00 rupee to 305.50.
